the myth of the ai race neither america nor china can achieve true tech dominance ss from essay by colin h kahl director and steven c hazy senior fellow at stanford universitys freeman spogli institute for international studies in july the trump administration released an artificial intelligence action plan titled winning the ai race which framed global competition over ai in stark terms whichever country achieves dominance in the technology will reap overwhelming economic military and geopolitical advantages as it did during the cold war with the space race or the nuclear buildup the us government is now treating ai as a contest with a single finish line and a single victor but that premise is misleading the united states and china the worlds two ai superpowers are not converging on the same path to ai leadership nor are they competing across a single dimension instead the ai competition is fragmenting across many domains including the development of the most advanced large language and multimodal models control over computing infrastructure such as data centers and topoftheline chips used to train and run models influence over which technologies and standards are used throughout the world and integration of ai into physical systems such as robots factories vehicles and military platforms having an edge in one area does not automatically translate into an advantage in the others as a result it is plausible that washington and beijing could each emerge as leaders in different parts of the ai ecosystem rather than one side decisively outpacing the other across the board

european commission gathering feedback on the importance of open source the european commission recently launched a call for evidence on a newer initiative about the importance of open source and their reliance on noneu countries as covered by cade the initiative is called towards european open digital ecosystems and it sets out how theyre trying to sort their approach towards the opensource sector across the european union from the official eu document they note how the new strategy will address the economic and political importance of open source as a crucial contribution to a strategic framework for eu technological sovereignty competitiveness and cybersecurity and that it will set out actions to strengthen the broader eu open ecosystem of solutions and products in critical sectors including internet technologies cloud artificial intelligence ai cybersecurity open hardware and industrial applications eg automotive and manufacturing the problems they want to tackle they say the eu faces a significant problem of dependence on noneu countries in the digital sphere which reduces users choice hampers eu companies competitiveness and can raise supply chain security issues as it makes it difficult to control our digital infrastructure both physical and software components potentially creating vulnerabilities including in critical sectors another thing they do highlight is that much of the value generated by opensource projects is exploited outside the eu often benefiting tech giants they go on to highlight various existing initiatives where the eu funds open source but they mention how supporting opensource communities solely through research and innovation programmes is not sufficient for successful upscaling and that it is critical to support emerging developer communities and businesses in scaling up via sustainable support and governance frameworks a lot of regular readers and people in the tech sector will already be very aware of all the issues especially with lots of big us tech giants reaping the benefits of open source with barely a contribution back its not difficult to see why the eu would want to break away from constantly relying on us tech especially with the current political climate too their key objectives continuing development and ensuring appropriate visibility of eu highquality and secure opensource solutions and demonstrating their added value addressing issues of deployment usability software supply chain security and governance maintenance of code and project sustainability to ensure takeup and upscaling supporting emerging opensource business and sustainability models for opensource companies and foundations including by developing publicprivate partnerships promoting best practice and encouraging the public sector specialised business sectors and large customers to contribute to and adopt open source and supporting market integration especially with legacy systems and policy alignment you can see the document for the consultation on the official eu website and if youre an eu citizen you can submit feedback on it too

artificial intelligence into individual cognition has exposed a widespread pattern of resistance across academic professional and online spaces this resistance often manifests as gatekeeping dismissal or moralized rejection of aiassisted workparticularly when such work originates outside traditional institutions this thesis argues that these responses are not primarily about accuracy ethics or rigor but about perceived threats to legitimacy authority and identity during a tooling transition ai functions as a cognitive multiplier collapsing historical barriers to synthesis and destabilizing legacy validation systems gatekeeping therefore should be understood as a defensive system response rather than an objective assessment of merit 1 introduction the repeated friction pattern across disciplines and platforms a recurring interaction has emerged an individual uses ai as a reasoning or synthesis tool produces coherent integrative or novel work encounters rejection framed as not rigorous not credible not original not valid because ai was involved this pattern appears regardless of correctness suggesting that the rejection precedes evaluation 2 historical role of gatekeeping gatekeeping historically served legitimate functions quality control fraud prevention credential signaling resource allocation however gatekeeping systems were designed for a world where access to synthesis was scarce expertise required institutional mediation tools were slow and asymmetric ai invalidates those assumptions 3 ai as a cognitive equalizer ai does not replace thinking it redistributes leverage capabilities that once required research teams libraries grant funding years of synthesis labor now require a capable mind iterative questioning tool fluency this shift removes the scarcity that gatekeeping relied upon 4 tool rejection as identity defense resistance to ai is often framed as concern about cheating laziness loss of standards epistemic collapse but structurally it functions as identity preservation my expertise is less special now authority preservation my credential is less decisive now role preservation my gate is no longer required this explains why aiassisted errors are magnified aiassisted successes are discounted tool usage is treated as moral failure rather than methodological choice 5 the asymmetry of scrutiny a key diagnostic feature of gatekeeping resistance is asymmetric evaluation humanonly work is judged on outcomes aiassisted work is judged on process purity this double standard reveals that the objection is not about truthbut about how truth is allowed to be produced 6 informal vs institutional cognition ai accelerates informal cognition public iteration crossdomain synthesis provisional frameworks open revision institutions remain optimized for slow validation narrow contributions credentialbased trust the conflict arises when informal cognition produces results before institutional validation can respond 7 social media as a stress test online platforms expose this conflict at scale good ideas without credentials are attacked novel synthesis is dismissed as ai slop requests for peer engagement are met with boundarypolicing instead of critique this is not because the work lacks merit but because the evaluator lacks a place to put it 8 why neurodivergent thinkers are hit first neurodivergent cognition often skips linear exposition favors system maps over stepwise proofs iterates publicly crosses domains freely when paired with ai this creates outputs that dont match expected form arrive too fast ignore implicit social pacing rules gatekeeping thus becomes a way to enforce cognitive conformity 9 predictive claim if this thesis is accurate we should observe increasing rejection of aiassisted work on moral grounds delayed institutional adaptation eventual normalization once authority structures adjust a generational divide in tool acceptance early resistance will be remembered not as cautionbut as inertia 10 conclusion gatekeeping and ai rejection are not signs of rigor they are symptoms of transition ai collapses historical barriers to synthesis forcing institutions and individuals to confront a difficult truth legitimacy is shifting from who you are to what you can demonstrate resistance is understandable but it is not sustainable the question is no longer whether ai will be integrated into human cognitionbut whether our validation systems will evolve fast enough to remain relevant

the mix and we end up with a technology capable of producing completely fabricated images with remarkably lifelike fidelity it has revolutionized the film industry making visual effects an integral part of the process motion capture deaging animation green screen backdrops overlaid with any environment required to sell the immersion of the story these are all forms of photo manipulation but there is a troubling downside deepfakes according to wikipedia deepfake is defined as images videos or audio that have been edited or generated using artificial intelligence aibased tools or audiovideo editing software what began as a form of entertainment is now not only capable of producing fictional content so believable its hard to detect where reality ends and it begins but is being used to spread misinformation and sexually exploit there is a laundry list of incidents and history stretching as far back as 2018 covering everything from satirical representations of various politicians to blackmail of those same public figures to the trend of creating pornography of celebrities without their knowledge or consent indeed the wiki page is headed by the warning that the louisville tackles permitting friction and better home buying affordability louisville is finally moving into the present and perhaps even the future by beginning to implement artificial intelligence inside its government systems mayor craig greenberg announced the citys first formal ai partnership teaming up with govstreamai to modernize the permitting process at the same time the city hired its first chief ai officer pamela mcknight who brings three decades of experience from intel most recently focused on ai adoption inside large organizations this isnt consumer ai hype its operational ai aimed squarely at one of the biggest friction points in local development permitting has long been a pain point for both residents and developers the govstream pilot is designed to reduce errors at the front end by checking applications against city code zoning rules floodplain data gis mapping and historic overlays before plans bounce back and forth for months in simple terms fewer surprises fewer resubmissions faster answers with people still making the final decisions this also feels long overdue a lot of people genuinely want to build good housing solutions and invest responsibly but the jefferson county permitting system has slowed projects down for years in many cases its been easier to invest outside the county entirely seeing the city acknowledge that friction and take a practical step to reduce it is encouraging this is exactly the kind of ai implementation that makes sense less bureaucracy fewer errors and more momentum toward actually improving housing outcomes beyond permitting louisville metro is exploring ai pilots in several areas infrastructure review potholes blight ada compliance 311 service routing and multilingual access redacting sensitive data for open records requests internal efficiency across a 5000employee organization this is part of a 2 million initiative to test where ai genuinely improves public service not replace it faster permitting lowers holding costs clearer guidance reduces legal risk less friction means capital can move where its needed into housing infrastructure and real improvements on the ground in regards to institutional ownership of singlefamily homes in louisville despite the narrative the singlefamily rental market is not dominated by giant institutions according to john burns research more than 76 of singlefamily rentals are owned by landlords with fewer than ten properties push the definition all the way up to owners with ninetynine homes and youre well past ninety percent the largest owners those with 1000 homes account for only a small singledigit share and yet they mattered disproportionately because markets arent shaped by who owns the most theyre shaped by who sets the marginal price for much of the last decade that marginal buyer was often a spreadsheet a national rentgrowth model applied locally when that buyer steps back not everywhere and not all at once the tone of the market changes apply the same logic locally greater louisville has roughly 55000 to 65000 singlefamily rental homes even under aggressive assumptions only a few thousand homes would realistically be affected by institutional pullback over time that means we should expect to see some additional inventory hit the market but not a flood this isnt what youre seeing in parts of alabama mississippi or georgia where rental supply grew faster institutional concentration ran higher and unwind pressure is showing up more visibly what changes here is subtler and healthier negotiations slow down inspections
